en: The Ritual Manual for the Brief Yoga Recitation of Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva,
composed by [the author whose titles were] Kaifu Yitongsi, Teci, Shih Hongluqing, and Duke of Suku.

The Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of Daxingshan Monastery—honored with a purple robe and the posthumous title of Minister of Works (Sikong), granted a fief of three thousand households, and bestowed the honorific name "Great Mirror of Correct Wisdom" (Dajian Zhenghao)—translates this by imperial decree: I shall now expound the Vajra Recitation Method of the Body, Speech, and Mind of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
By practicing this dharma, one becomes equal to Vajrasattva;
the practitioner dwells on the stage of conduct through resolute belief (adhimukti-caryā-bhūmi) and has previously entered the Great Maṇḍala of the Vajradhātu.
Having received the bodhicitta vow,
one possesses great compassion for all sentient beings and the resolve to deliver them and establish them in peace and happiness.
Without begrudging body or life,
one should constantly, from moment to moment, maintain the aspiration to attain the body of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
and diligently practice this within the activity of the body.
He beheld all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas as if they were right before his eyes,
dwelling within the mountain hermitages and *āraṇyakas*.
Whether in a private chamber, a monastery,
or a residence, one should establish a *maṇḍala*,
facing either east or west, whichever is most convenient.
With body upright, sit in the full-lotus posture—either the complete lotus, the Samantabhadra lotus, or in a comfortable posture.
With the mind, universally take all realms of sentient beings as the object of focus.
To purify the three karmas of body, speech, and mind of these sentient beings, the secret mantra says:
Oṃ svabhāva-śuddhāḥ sarvadharmāḥ svabhāva-śuddho ’ham. Next, one should visualize the Tathāgata’s marks and signs as perfectly complete, and mentally offer worship.
With celestial, exquisite unguents, flower garlands, incense, lamps, food, and drink, and with various forms of praise,
one should perform worship according to the four types of prostrations, mudrās, and secret mantras,
offering up one's own body as an oblation to the Tathāgatas of the four directions.
Then, having accomplished the restraint of the precepts of unimpeded wisdom regarding the three periods of time,
one should rise and place the right knee upon the ground,
binding and maintaining the Vajra-samaya-mudrā.
Recite with focused attention and scatter [the flowers] upon the crown of the head.
By forming this mudrā and reciting the mantra, [the rite is accomplished].
Then, the secret mantra for universally performing prostrations, making offerings, and rendering service to all Tathāgatas is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-kavaca. Next, one should confess and reveal one's transgressions.
Having performed the rejoicing, the request [for teaching], the dedication, and the making of vows, one then sits in the full lotus posture (*paryaṅka*) and reflects as follows:
"May all sentient beings attain the supramundane, unsurpassed *siddhi*. The secret mantra is: [insert mantra].
Oṃ sarvatathāgataśāsana-sarvasattvānāṃ sarvasiddhyarthaṃ paridhāraya tathāgataśāsanadṛḍha svāhā. Next, bind the vajra-palmya-mudrā.
Recite the mantra three times.
The mantra is: Oṃ vajra-jvālaya. While reciting this mantra, form this mudrā.
All siddhis corresponding to the yoga practiced through these gateways shall be accomplished. Forming the vajra-bond mudrā, recite the mantra:
Vajra-bandha. By this, all fetters shall be liberated.
The ten pāramitās are instantaneously brought to full perfection.
Next, one performs the binding mudrā with three pulls,
strikes the chest, and recites the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ vajra-bandha traṭ! By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, one should enter the maṇḍala; the ācārya shall lead one in.
The Vajrasattva of the three vajra-actions enters the disciple’s heart,
causing the innate vajra-wisdom to be activated and manifest.
Next, bind the Vajra-Praveśa mudrā. This is the same as the previous vajra-bond;
insert both thumbs into the palms between the ring fingers and recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajraveśa huṃ. By forming this mudrā,
the Vajra of the Three Activities performs the great āveśa within the body.
One obtains great spiritual efficacy and majestic virtue.
Next, using the same mudrā as before,
bend each of the two index fingers so that they rest against the backs of the two thumbs.
Then, form the Vajra-fist mudrā and recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajramuṣṭi maṃ. By binding this seal, one causes the three activities to abide as firm vajras, without dispersal or loss.
Next, join the previous Vajrabandha mudrā and extend the two middle fingers upright.
This is the Vajrasattva mudrā; the secret mantra is:
Oṃ vajrasamayas tvam. By binding this seal, [the rite is accomplished].
The practitioner should abide in the samādhi of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Seated upon a lunar disc,
they should cause the physical form and radiance of their body to be perfectly complete.
Next, form the Great Vow Truth Seal of Surata:
with the bound seal, join the tips of the two thumbs and the two little fingers together,
like a single-pronged vajra.
Insert the two middle fingers into the palms and join them upright;
by placing them against the heart, it is accomplished.
One should then perform this contemplation.
Once my body has become that of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva,
at the moment this mind is generated, I shall achieve boundless liberation and contemplate all sentient beings as being indistinguishable from myself and others.
The great compassion of identical essence consists in reciting the true secret mantra of the great vow:
*Oṃ vajrasamaya hūṃ sara tathātvam*. Next, one should abide in the supreme samādhi of the Wrathful Vajra of the Three Times.
Standing in the mudrā, with four faces and eight arms, his majestic majesty blazes forth;
his radiance is so intense it is like the conflagration at the end of an aeon.
His left foot treads upon Maheśvara.
With the right foot treading upon Umā,
one should immediately form two vajra-fists with both hands,
hooking the two little fingers together in a reversed manner.
Extend both index fingers.
By rotating the mudrā counter-clockwise, one expels all māras of humans and devas, as well as those who create obstacles;
by rotating it clockwise, one establishes the boundaries of the cardinal and intermediate directions.
Even the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas do not transgress this;
how much less so those who create obstacles within the triple world?
Thereupon, one seals the four places—the heart, forehead, throat, and crown—with the mudrā, reciting the secret mantra as follows:
Oṃ suṃbha niḥsuṃbha hūṃ | gṛhṇa gṛhṇa hūṃ | gṛhṇāpaya hūṃ | ānaya hoḥ | bhagavan vajra hūṃ phaṭ. While forming this mudrā, recite the mantra, bringing the three secrets into correspondence.
All the seeds of affliction within the ālayavijñāna are completely incinerated by this vajra-fire of wisdom.
No external obstacles whatsoever shall be able to act as hindrances or difficulties.
Next, bind the Samaya-mudrā of the Lotus Family:
form the Vajra-bond with both hands.
Joining the two thumbs and the two little fingers together, place the mudrā at the mouth.
Visualize yourself as the Bodhisattva Vajradharma, and recite the secret mantra: [insert mantra].
Oṃ vajrasamayasarvva vaṃ. By binding this mudrā, all the samādhi-yogas one has cultivated will manifest before one.
Next, bind the mudrā of concentration.
Survey the Buddhas throughout the entirety of space as being like sesame seeds.
Then, recite the secret mantra, saying:
Oṃ sarvayogacittam utpādayāmi. By forming this mudrā and reciting this mantra, all obstacles are extinguished.
One attains peace, happiness, and joy;
transcends the realm of Māra;
and, like all Buddhas, receives offerings from all the gods of the world.
Then he recited the secret mantra of the penetrating mind:
Oṃ citta-prativedhaṃ karomi. This is the wisdom of the samādhi of the ninefold dependent origination.
One contemplates all phenomena as being like an illusion,
like a mirage, like a dream, like a reflection, like an echo, like a shadow, like the moon in water, like a magical transformation, and like space.
Having made this contemplation,
this mind— regarding both defilement and purity—
is unimpeded in its penetration, just like empty space.
Next, one should enter the visualization of bodhicitta.
Recite the secret mantra of bodhicitta:
Oṃ bodhicittam utpādayāmi. While forming this mudrā, place it upon the body at the center of the chest.
Contemplate the full moon as bright, pure, and cool.
Having completed the recitation of the mantra of the bodhicitta many times until it is thoroughly mastered,
the water of the mind becomes clear and pure.
The reflection of the moon of bodhicitta appears within it;
upon this full moon,
one visualizes a five-pronged vajra.
Reciting the secret mantra with complete clarity, one should recite it while performing this visualization: *Oṃ tiṣṭha vajra jūḥ*. Thus one recites this secret mantra.
This mind becomes like a vajra.
Next, visualize the body as a five-pronged vajra and recite the mantra:
*vajratmakūṃ*. Then, visualize the Buddhas filling the entirety of space.
All [elements] enter into the vajra and merge into a single essence.
By means of such contemplative wisdom (*vipaśyanā*) and the recitation of the secret mantra (*mantra*),
the three karmas of the practitioner become like a vajra.
The practitioner should contemplate their own body as that of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva:
wearing the crown of the five Buddhas, with a body like the color of crystal and moonlight,
and holding a five-pronged vajra in the right hand.
Holding a vajra bell in the left hand,
with the body situated within a full moon mandala,
recite the secret mantra clearly and distinctly:
Oṃ vajrasattva samutthaṃ haṃ. Next, employ the Suvarṇavajra mudrā:
form the vajra-bond (*vajrabandha*).
Insert the right thumb into the left "tiger's mouth" (the hollow between the thumb and forefinger) and it is accomplished.
With this mudrā, empower the heart, forehead, throat, and crown;
the secret mantra is: Oṃ surata saṃtvaṃ. Then, with both hands, perform the vajra-bind.
Extend the two middle fingers and bend their upper joints like swords;
bend each of the two index fingers and place them alongside the two middle fingers so that they touch.
When the two thumbs are joined like the *paryaṅka* (cross-legged) posture, it is formed.
This is called the Vajradhātu-mudrā;
it is also called the Five-Buddha-Crown Mudrā. Its secret mantra is as follows:
Oṃ sarvatathāgata-ratna-viśodhaya āḥ. Next, bind the consecration mudrā and place it upon the crown of the head; with the same mudrā as before, the secret mantra is: [as above].
Oṃ vajramale bhiścaḥ maṃ vaṃ. Next, form the vajra-fists with both hands and place them at the forehead as if tying on a garland of silk.
Next, having tied it behind the head as before,
let it flow down from the little fingers in the manner of trailing silken ribbons.
Recite the secret mantra:
Oṃ. Next, perform the Armor Seal (*kavaca-mudrā*): form two vajra-fists with both hands and extend the two index fingers.
Visualize the two syllables Oṃ and Chin on the tips of the fingers,
then place the two fingers at the heart and circle them three times.
Next, from behind, move back to the navel and the two knees;
again, reach the navel, then the waist, and back to the heart.
Then the left and right shoulders and neck, followed by the crown of the head, the back of the forehead, and the back of the skull.
Form fists as if in the gesture of fastening armor. The mantra is:
Oṃ āpāye vajrakavaca bandhara kṣaiṃ hūṃ haḥ kaṃ. Next, rotate the two fists as if in a dancing gesture and clap once to bring about joy. The mantra is: [as above].
Oṃ vajra-tuṣya hūṃ. Next, bind the seal of the Vajracakra Maṇḍala:
form two vajra-fists with both hands.
The seal is formed by interlocking the two index fingers and the two little fingers.
Regarding the mudrā, the body, and the five locations, the secret mantra is:
Oṃ vajra-cakra hūṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ. Next, perform the seal for awakening all the noble assemblies.
Crossing the two hands at the arms with the right over the left, snap the fingers;
snap the fingers once for each recitation, completing four repetitions. The secret mantra is as follows:
"Oṃ vajrasamāja jaḥ jaḥ. As soon as this mudrā was formed,
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and his entire retinue gathered like clouds in the sky at that very moment.
Next is the ritual for binding the mudrās of the four gate Bodhisattvas. First, at the eastern gate is the Bodhisattva Vajrāṅkuśa, who resides in the center of the maṇḍala and is blue in color.
At the southern gate is the Bodhisattva Vajrapāśa.
The yellow one has the mudrā of holding a cord;
in the western gate is Vajrasphoṭā Bodhisattvī,
red in color, with the mudrā of holding a chain.
In the center of the northern gate is the Bodhisattva Vajraghaṇṭā.
She is green in color and holds a bell as her mudrā.
Each of these four bodhisattvas is adorned with a crown of the five buddhas and various other exquisite ornaments.
To serve as an adornment,
next form the hook seal (*aṅkuśamudrā*): with both hands in vajra-fists,
hook the two little fingers together with their tips facing inward.
Extend the left index finger straight upward.
Bend the right index finger and move it up and down.
This is the Hook Mudrā; its secret mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajra-kuśe (1). Without releasing the previous mudrā, join the tips of the two index fingers together like a ring;
this is the pāśa-mudrā. The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajrapāśi hūṃ. With the previous mudrā, cross the two index fingers and the two thumbs at their tips, pressing them together, and bend the arms.
The secret mantra for this *śṛṅkhalā-mudrā* is:
Oṃ vajra-śaṅkarī hūṃ. Perform the *śṛṅkhalā-mudrā* as before; insert both thumbs into the palms and shake them.
Then, the secret mantra is recited as follows:
*Oṃ vajra-gaṇe hūṃ*. Next, one recites the one hundred and eight names of the honored Bodhisattva.
Having finished the recitation, one then binds the Great Vow of Truth Seal of Vajrasattva.
And recite the secret mantra to invite the assembly of noble ones to descend into the maṇḍala.
The secret mantra is: *HĪ MAHĀSUKHA VAJRA SATTVAYA HĪ*.
Dvi-ṣṭi-glin (2) samaya-mahā-sukha-vajra-mukha-samaya-maṇḍalāya pramuñca pramuñca sārāt sattvaṃ ānarakto 'ham.
Bhava 8. Suduṣyaṃ bhava 9. Sunirvṛtaṃ bhava 10. Supūryaṃ bhava 11.
Bhagavan 12. Anandinidhanaḥ sattva 13. Sa...
VAŚINTIṂ PRAYACCHĀSTVAM AKLIṢṬA-PRABHEṢAYA SAMAYAROMAṆṬAKA VAŚIKAROMI.
18. Samayamudrā | 19. Pūrṇatrapāṇi | 20. Jyok | 21. Hūṃ | 22. Vaṃ | 23.
Hoḥ | Having formed the mudrās, recite these secret mantras.
This mudrā and mantra are able to awaken Samantabhadra Bodhisattva and his assembly of holy retinues,
causing them to descend to the site of practice with joyful hearts, never transgressing their original vows.
This mudrā and mantra...
One is able to summon, lead in, bind, and cause [the deity] to rejoice.
Reciting until the syllable *jvaḥ*,
move two fingers within the palms like hooks back and forth.
When reaching the syllable HŪṂ, it is bent like a ring, forming a noose; reaching the syllable VAṂ, they are interlaced, which is called a chain;
reaching the syllable HOḤ, they move like ringing bells, able to delight all the noble ones.
Recite [the mantra] either three times or four times.
Next, form the argha mudrā with both hands in the vajra-palms gesture.
Join the tips of the two middle fingers together.
Place the two index fingers behind the middle fingers in the shape of a hook.
Then, each of the two thumbs presses against the base of its respective index finger; thus it is formed.
Holding the arghya vessel with the mudrā,
one should offer it at the forehead.
If there is no arghya previously present within the maṇḍala, [one should prepare it].
Simply change [the previous mudrā] so that the two thumbs are crossed;
this constitutes the Argha-mudrā.
Visualize the water of eight qualities bathing the feet of all the Honored Ones of the Noble Assembly. The secret mantra is as follows:
Paramasūkṣaśāye (1) sakhrida (2) vilāsanimidranamama vipaghaṃ jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ (4) hi hi hi hi (5) pratīccha (6) kusumāñjalīraṇata. Because of this offering of arghya.
This can wash away the dust and grime of afflictions from beginningless time,
swiftly attaining purity of body, speech, and mind.
Next, perform the outer offerings to the various deities.
The Bodhisattva Priyadarśana in the southeast holds two vajra-fists at his heart;
the Bodhisattva Vajrahāsa in the southwest holds two fists at his sides, with the hands splayed backward.
In the northwest, the Bodhisattva Vajragītā forms a fist with her left hand;
she extends her arm upward and points the index finger toward her body, holding a vīṇā as her mudrā.
The right hand makes the gesture of plucking a string.
To the northeast is Vajranṛtyā Bodhisattva,
who forms the dance mudrā by rotating two fists.
The attire and forms of these four deities are all golden, like those in the initial *hikṣepa-mudrā*.
With both fists encircling the heart,
rotate them to the left and right while reciting the secret mantra as follows:
Kīradivajravilāsini traṭ. Next, form the laughter mudrā (*hāsa-mudrā*): as with the previous mudrā, place it beside the mouth and turn the palms outward.
Gradually opening from the little fingers,
each disperses toward the back.
Abiding in a smiling expression, recite the secret mantra:
*Kīra-ti-vajra hāse ha ha*. Next, form a fist with the right hand, extend the index finger,
and bend the arm toward the body like a *vīṇā* lute.
Form a fist with the right hand and extend the index finger upright,
making the gesture of plucking a string;
this is the mudrā of song.
The secret instruction says:
*Khīradivajra* (1) *nitīti* (2) *tititi* (3). With both fists, rotate and dance from the heart;
gradually ascending to the crown of the head, join the palms and then open them.
The secret mantra of this dance mudrā is:
*khīradivajra nṛtya ve phaṭ phaṭ*. Next, one forms the cloud-vajra bodhisattva incense-offering mudrā.
Place the two fists side by side;
when cast downward, the seal is formed.
Visualize this deity in the southeast corner of the inner court of the mandala.
Both the attire and the form are entirely black, holding an incense burner as one's seal.
Having performed this visualization, recite the secret mantra:

Oṃ maṅgava-jri gulu gulu. Next, with both fists initially positioned as if dancing, then bring the two fists together with the palms facing upward in the manner of scattering flowers; this is the seal of the Bodhisattva Vasantavajra.
One should visualize this Honored One residing in the southwest corner of the inner court, with both complexion and robes white, holding a flower.
The secret mantra is: Oṃ mātuvajri hūṃ hūṃ. Next, perform the lamp mudrā of the Bodhisattva Autumn Vajra.
With both fists held upright, extend the two thumbs; one should then visualize this Honored One residing in the northwest corner of the inner courtyard.
His form and attire are entirely red, and he holds a lamp as his mudrā.
The secret mantra is:
Oṃ śaraṇavajri āḥ āḥ. Next, bind the mudrā of the Bodhisattva Vajramegha:
place both fists face down and touch them to the chest.
Disperse the visualization in both directions, imagining this Honored One residing in the northeast corner of the inner courtyard.
His form and attire are entirely green.
He holds an incense box; the secret mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vajraśikhari hūṃ hūṃ hūṃ. Next, within the center of the maṇḍala, one should visualize a full moon disk;
within that moon disk is the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
Abiding in the Vajragarva-mudrā,
one next visualizes Kāmacakra before the Great Sage;
his form and attire are red in color.
Adorned with robes, crowns, garlands, necklaces, and various ornaments,
he gazes upon the Great Sage who abides in the mudrā of the adamantine bow and arrow.
Next, to the right of the Great Sage, [is...]
Visualize the Honored One Kīlikīla;
his color is white, and he stands with his two vajra-fists crossed at the chest in the *āliṅgana-mudrā* (embrace seal).
Next, following the Great Sage,
one should visualize Rāgavajrī,
whose form and attire are entirely blue.
He raises his left arm to grasp the makara banner,
supporting its elbow with his right hand,
likewise holding the banner together with him.
To the left of the Great Sage,
visualize the Honored One Vajramāna;
his form and attire are entirely yellow.
Place the two vajra-fists at the navel;
incline the head slightly to the left.
These five deities all abide in the mudrā of the karma-samādhi.
Next, the mantra of Vajraghoṣa is:
*Jaya vajra nṛśeṣaja samatāṭaṭa*. Next, recite the secret mantra of the Honored One Kīlikīla:
HŪṂ VAJRAHEKARE KĪLI HŪṂ. Then, recite the secret mantra of Vajrarāga:
VAṂ VAJRĀNĪ SAMARĀTA. Next, recite the secret mantra of Mānavajra:
HŪṂ VAJRA KĀMINĪ TĀRAM. [The above seventeen deities of the noble assembly are depicted with their respective forms, garments, and flower seats within moon disks.]
Furthermore, one's own body abides as the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā),
surrounded by the assembly of noble deities;
all of these must be clearly visualized.
Next, one should recite the praise to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva as follows:
*Sarvanugāsukha-sattvānāṃ tvaṃ vajrasattvaparamasurata pravartaya mahāsukhanirjitarājāryaja pratisiddhinyasicyadhara upadrava*. Recite the first line of this praise.
One should form the Vajra-karma mudrā of Desire and then recite the second line; next,
one forms the Kīlikīla-vajra-karma mudrā.
Next, for the third phrase,
one binds the Vajra-karma-mudrā of Attachment.
For the fourth phrase:
Having bound the Vajra-karma mudrā of pride,
one then accomplishes the four kinds of song and the four kinds of dance mudrās.
This is to be employed when entering the Great Samādhi while reciting praises.
Next, recite the true secret mantra of the Mahāyāna Amoghasamaya:
Oṃ mahāsukha-vajrasattva jjaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ surata-satva vaṃ. Abide in the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā).
One becomes equal to Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
If one wishes to accomplish the sādhana of the deity, one should recite for one month,
reciting an unlimited number of times during each of the four periods of the day.
If you become fatigued, release the mudrā,
join your palms in the all-pervading vajra gesture (sarvakāyavajra-añjali), and pay homage;
use this as a period of rest.
One should cause the mind to remain free from weariness.
On a night of the full moon, one should bind the Great Seal (mahāmudrā) and perform recitation throughout the night until dawn.
Samantabhadra Bodhisattva arrives;
his body, radiant like a lunar disc, embraces the practitioner’s own person and enters into all their limbs.
The practitioner’s body becomes identical to that of Samantabhadra;
wearing the five-Buddha crown and adorned with celestial, exquisite necklaces and flower garlands,
their body, speech, and mind become like those of Vajrasattva.
When all their kinsmen saw that person manifest such majestic power,
they were all struck with wonder and paid him respectful homage.
That person constantly performed great supernatural feats within his own home.
He also manifests in the form of a Buddha, displaying great supernormal powers;
he also manifests the supreme Vajra-body of the three times,
subduing all who are difficult to subdue, so that they are all brought under control.
Rising into the air at will,
they travel freely through immeasurable worlds to make offerings to all Buddhas.
Experiencing the sublime pleasures of the five celestial desires,
may their lifespan be as vast as space,
and may they bring benefit and happiness to infinite sentient beings.
The Ritual Manual for the Concise Yoga Recitation of Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva, which Accomplishes Great Benefit and Attains the Body of Vairocana Buddha.
